title: Arrival at Outpost Echo

beats.narrativeText: The learner arrives at the deserted Outpost Echo research station.

Although everything appears quiet, the station clearly shows signs of previous activity — equipment remains where it was left, doors are unlocked, and observation boards still display unfinished notes.
Atlas helps the learner perform an initial survey of the station, exploring the map and labelling important areas.
The learner records unusual observations while exploring, noticing the first hints that something is not quite right.
The learner must produce a simple sketch map of the station using their own observations.
The completed sketch map reveals the layout of Outpost Echo clearly for the first time.
The learner reflects on what the untouched equipment and unfinished notes might mean.
As the survey ends, the first real hints of mystery begin to appear.

activities.title: Explore Station Map
activities.storyContext: Atlas provides a basic map of Outpost Echo to help the learner begin their initial survey.
activities.instructions: Walk through the station map with Atlas, noting the main areas and how they connect.
activities.output: A list of the station's main areas in the Explorer Journal.

activities.title: Label Important Areas
activities.storyContext: Knowing the station's layout will help later investigations.
activities.instructions: Label the important areas of the station map, such as the laboratory, observatory and living quarters.

activities.title: Record Unusual Observations
activities.storyContext: Equipment remains where it was left, and observation boards still display unfinished notes.
activities.instructions: Record anything unusual you notice about the station in your Explorer Journal.

activities.title: Produce a Simple Sketch Map
activities.storyContext: A clear map will help the learner navigate Outpost Echo in future missions.
activities.instructions: Draw a simple sketch map of the station based on your survey.
activities.output: A hand-drawn sketch map of Outpost Echo.

activities.title: Improve the Station Map
activities.storyContext: A well-made map uses symbols so anyone can read it quickly.
activities.instructions: Add symbols and a key to your sketch map to make it easier to read.
activities.output: An improved sketch map with a symbol key.

activities.title: How Are Research Stations Organised?
activities.storyContext: Outpost Echo was built to follow the same principles as real research stations.
activities.instructions: Find out how a real scientific research station is organised and compare it with Outpost Echo.
activities.output: None required — this is an open investigation.

prompts: What did you notice about Outpost Echo that made you feel like something was left unfinished?

discussionPoints: What did the station's layout tell you about how the expedition worked?
What would you want to explore first if you arrived somewhere new?
parentGuide.preparation: No special preparation required. A ruler is useful for the sketch map.
parentGuide.assessment: Look for a clearly labelled sketch map and specific, descriptive observations rather than vague statements.

completionCriteria: Station map explored, important areas labelled, and a sketch map produced.
